title: Breaking: The Snow That Stayed
description: It snows for the first time ever in a town that has never been cold, and Snazzie FM covers the half-inch like a fallout event. Rhonda insists it is textbook water right up until her thermometer hits forty and the snow refuses to melt, Sal sells it by the bag at a climbing price, and Winston claims he predicted it and therefore owns it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We are interrupting the regular hour on Snazzie FM for a breaking surface event. For the first time in recorded town history, there is a white substance on the ground. <p:0.3> Do not touch the white substance.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, it's snow.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We have not confirmed that, Barry. We're calling it the substance until the experts weigh in. Rhonda, you're our meteorologist. What are we looking at?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: So, good news. It's textbook. <p:0.3> It's water, Ronnie, just cold water, in a tidy little crystal. Half an inch. It'll be gone by lunch, this is the most normal thing in the world.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: See? It melts. That is the whole thing snow does, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie, it's Sal. <p:0.3> I'm out here bagging it. Twenty a bag, cash, it is GOING fast, it is the only snow in the county.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Sal, this is an active surface event, you should not be monetizing it.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Active events are when you monetize, Ronnie. Supply and demand. Twenty a bag.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Excuse me. As I have said for YEARS, this town would one day go cold. I predicted this snow. Which makes it, legally, MY snow.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You can't own snow, Winston.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: You can own what you foresee, Barry. I'll be wanting a plaque. <p:0.3> And a deed.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Okay, small update. <p:0.3> The thermometer says forty and it is still here. Which is fine. That is fine. Forty is, technically, above the temperature it should melt at.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It should be melting at forty, Rhonda.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: It SHOULD be, Barry, yes. <p:0.3> The textbook is very clear. The snow has just elected not to.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hi, dear. I've got some on my porch and I've decided to keep it. <p:0.3> I named it. It's behaving. It won't come inside, won't leave. Just sits.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, do not name the substance. Naming it makes it a resident.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Too late, dear. His name is Kevin. He's very polite.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks, based on a non-melting forty-degree event, I am upgrading us to a Tier Two Surface Condition. <p:0.3> Bring in your pets. Do not name your snow.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Ronnie, given the Tier Two, I'm adjusting. <p:0.3> It's forty a bag now. It's a different market.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It doubled? It's the same snow, Sal!

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: It's RARER snow now, Barry. Same snow, scarier paperwork.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: He cannot SELL my snow, Ronnie. I predicted it. Every bag Sal moves is theft of my foresight!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Tiny correction, everyone. <p:0.3> The thermometer just hit fifty-five. The snow is, if anything, looking comfortable.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Comfortable? Snow does not get comfortable, Rhonda!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Kevin's settling in, dear. I gave him a little fence.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: If it's not melting then it's PERMANENT inventory! <p:0.3> Name your price! Name it!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: The price is a DEED, Sal! In MY name!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's water, Winston!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: It's textbook water!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: His name is Kevin!

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: I leased a THOUSAND BAGS!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Everybody hold. <p:0.3> Rhonda. Give me the number.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: So, Ronnie. <p:0.4> The thermometer reads sixty-eight. The snow is not melting. <p:0.3> And it has spread one inch past where it landed. Overnight. On its own.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It moved. <p:0.4> Folks, I'm reclassifying it. This is no longer a weather event. <p:0.3> It's a resident.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Does anybody want to buy a thousand bags of permanent snow? <p:0.3> Anybody? <p:0.4> ...Hello?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Nobody's buying snow that won't melt, Sal.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, there it is, folks. The town's first snow, and it has decided to stay. <p:0.3> Winston, you wanted the deed. <p:0.4> It's moving an inch a night. It's all yours.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Ronnie? <p:0.3> Quick one. Which way is the inch headed?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Toward us, Ronnie. <p:0.3> It's in the parking lot.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Kevin says hello, dear.
